meta.description: Master registry of all GPCV (General Purpose Conceptionary Vocabulary) templates. Each entry maps a template file to its path type, learning track, supported language pairs, and pedagogical metadata.
meta.author: Alan William Preston

phonographic.description: Templates for phonographic / romanized-alphabet languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Bahasa Indonesia, Te Reo Māori, etc.)

logographic.description: Templates for logographic / non-romanized languages (Japanese, Mandarin Chinese, Korean, etc.)

templates.description: A single vertical line representing a stable, unchanging state. Vocabulary items positioned along the line.
A single horizontal line with 5 vocabulary positions. PLANNED — file not yet created for phonographic track. Logographic equivalent: LOG-HL-5TB-Generic.html already exists.
templates.notes: Logographic track has both 5TB and 10TB variants. Phonographic track currently has only 10TB. A 5TB phonographic variant may be created when needed.

templates.description: A single horizontal line with 10 evenly-spaced vocabulary positions. Represents a continuum or spectrum.
templates.notes: The only horizontal line template currently in the phonographic track. A 5TB variant (ROM-HL-5TB-Generic.html) is planned but not yet created.

templates.description: A diagonal line rising left to right, representing gradual increase or improvement.
A diagonal line falling left to right, representing gradual decrease or decline.
Five horizontal lines with instant (vertical) transitions between them. Change is sudden; the state is temporary (returns to baseline).
Inverted version of IT5L — five lines descending then returning. Represents a sudden temporary drop.
Three lines with instant upward transitions that are permanent — the level does not return to baseline.
Three lines with instant downward transitions that are permanent.
Five lines with gradual (diagonal) transitions and continuation paths on Lines 1 and 3. 7 vocabulary positions including continuations.
Expanded version of GT5L with 11 vocabulary positions for more detailed annotation.
suitable_for: gradual temporary changes with detailed vocabulary

templates.description: Inverted version of GT5L — gradual descent and return. Represents a temporary dip or trough.
Three lines with gradual upward transitions. Each new level is permanent.
Three lines with gradual downward transitions. Each new level is permanently lower.
A bell-shaped curve — rises to a peak then returns to baseline. 19 states along the curve plus 10 transition positions.

An inverted bell curve with a wide trough — descends gradually to a broad low point then returns to baseline. Both phonographic GTCVI variants (Wide and Shallow) now exist, matching the logographic track.
templates.notes: Fixed 2026-07-10: mode-separated learned-item tracking (learnedItemsStates/learnedItemsTransitions) to stop Transitions-mode quiz answers bleeding into States-mode display; fixed a drag-reachability bug where an unconditional alternating vertical offset made every 'below'-positioned unlearned item permanently unreachable (exceeded activationDistance); learned items now alternate above/below the curve — matching the pattern used in ROM-DU-Generic — only once already learned. User-tested and confirmed working by Alan.

templates.description: An inverted bell curve with a shallow trough — a minor dip that returns quickly to baseline. Built 2026-07-09 from ROM-GTCVI-Wide's scaffolding, combined with LOG-GTCVI-Shallow's curve geometry (half the dip depth, higher baseline, same width). Logographic equivalent: LOG-GTCVI-Shallow-Generic.html.
templates.notes: Same fixes applied as ROM-GTCVI-Wide (mode-separated learned arrays, drag-reachability fix). User-tested and confirmed working by Alan.

templates.description: A curve that rises to a new permanently-higher baseline. Represents permanent improvement after a peak.
A curve that descends to a new permanently-lower baseline.

A horizontal line with a visually distinct neutral centre point and two opposing poles. The draggable circle starts at neutral and moves left (negative pole) or right (positive pole), with its fill colour interpolating along a configurable three-colour spectrum (negative → neutral → positive). 4+1+4 = 9 textbox positions arranged in a cosine arc (extremes high, centre near the line) to prevent overlap. This is the default template for ARCHILEXEME concepts — concepts whose natural structure is a neutral zero-point flanked by two opposite extremes (e.g. Temperature, Weight, Appetite, Mood).
templates.notes: Archilexeme default template. Always confirm the concept card is named after the archilexeme (the neutral parent term), not one pole — e.g. 'Appetite' not 'Hunger'. The centre-cross transition item marks the semantic moment of passing through the normal/neutral state. Frame colour spectrum is configurable per-instance (frame_colour_neg / frame_colour_neutral / frame_colour_pos in LANG block) — four suggested natural spectrums are documented in the template comments (Acoustic/Light, Humidity, Psych/Energy, Material).
suitable_for: any concept with a neutral midpoint and two opposing extremes

templates.description: An inverted bell-curve shape with flat shoulders at the top (entry/exit points), descending smoothly through a full-width dashed normal-state line at 50% page height, to a nadir at the bottom centre representing the most intense state. Mirrors back up symmetrically to the opposite top corner. Unlike ROM-HL-BI, this template visually implies the journey/process of intensifying and returning to normal — the curve shape itself carries pedagogical meaning (continuation, cyclicality) that a straight line does not. 4 textboxes down the left side, 1 at the bottom (most intense), 4 up the right side.
templates.notes: Use when the concept has a clear single most-intense state reached via a gradual process (not a static bidirectional spectrum) — e.g. illness severity, hunger/satiety cycling, emotional intensity peaking and subsiding. The bottom point is always the MOST INTENSE/negative state by convention. Sliding text in Transitions mode is directly draggable (no separate hit-area rectangle) — click-and-drag the text itself, following the pattern established in GTCV.html. Frame colour spectrum (frame_colour_top / frame_colour_bottom) is configurable per-instance.
suitable_for: any concept with one clear most-intense state reached via a process

templates.description: An analogue clock face with dynamic text arrays for greetings, approximate time, exact time, and part of day. Time-based sentence generation driven by grammar rules.
templates.notes: Requires grammar-rule functions (formatExact, formatApprox) — not a simple vocabulary array. See LANG config block.

templates.description: A colour-coded 60-segment clock ring. Each minute segment is clickable and launches a quiz on the corresponding time expression. Covers exact minutes, quarter/half past, approaching/just-gone landmarks.
A circular dial representing the 24-hour tidal cycle with states and transitions modes.
A circular dial with 8 segments representing the named parts of the 24-hour day (dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, evening, night etc.).
A circular dial with 7 segments for days of the week. Sun-cycle arc decoration toggleable. Draggable sun frame.
A 12-segment circular calendar with optional seasons overlay. Supports 2-season (tropical) and 4-season (temperate) overlays via configurable seasonsData.
A two-segment circular template for climates with a wet season and a dry season. 8 vocabulary positions. Suitable for tropical monsoon climates worldwide.
Four-quadrant seasonal template aligned to the Southern Hemisphere calendar: Dec-Feb=Summer, Mar-May=Autumn, Jun-Aug=Winter, Sep-Nov=Spring. Includes significant dates/events category.
Four-quadrant seasonal template aligned to the Northern Hemisphere calendar: Dec-Feb=Winter, Mar-May=Spring, Jun-Aug=Summer, Sep-Nov=Autumn.
A 29.5-day spring/neap tidal cycle on a circular dial. Four alternating quadrants (spring/neap). 12 states + 12 transitions distributed at 30° intervals.
A 28-day lunar phase cycle. 28 moon-phase icons (rendered via SVG clip-paths) around the ring; 8 vocabulary positions for the named phases.
A general-purpose 28-position circular cycle template, originally designed for the menstrual cycle. Colour-banded marker ring with Display All toggle. 8 vocabulary positions.
templates.notes: General-purpose 28-day cycle — not limited to menstrual cycle. Suitable for any 28-day/28-stage recurring concept.

templates.description: A 16-point compass rose on a circular dial. 360 degree markers on the rim. Four colour-coded quadrants. Draggable compass arrow.
A rotating SVG steering wheel. 20 directional phrases activated as the wheel turns. 3-level click cycle per phrase (TL → SL → Quiz). Display-all toggle cycles through 3 states.
templates.notes: 2026-07-11: Added App.html injection support (whole-LANG-object replacement, same strategy as HL-BI/CV-BI but with CR-SW's own field set and block-comment /* ... */ end-of-config marker, not HL-BI/CV-BI's line-comment style). Fixed instructions panel defaulting to TL instead of SL — a beginner can't read target-language instructions before learning the target language, unlike vocabulary which is meant to be revealed progressively. Both fixes are at the generic-template level, apply to any future concept using this template. Vocabulary items are stored as an array of OBJECTS (not arrays), keyed by angle {a, tl, sl, py, posA, dy} — py/posA/dy are template-tuned label-placement offsets that must be preserved from the generic template's own V array when building a concept card, not regenerated.

Logographic variant of ROM-HL-BI. Same neutral-centre bidirectional structure, with the 4-level click cycle (TLR default → TL script → SL → Quiz) used throughout the logographic track. Quiz tests TLR (romanized) input with diacritic-tolerant normalization via AnswerUtils, since learners cannot type logographic characters directly.
templates.notes: Archilexeme default template for logographic languages. Same design principles as ROM-HL-BI — concept cards must be named after the archilexeme, not a pole. Each conceptData/transitionsData item carries an additional TLR field (5th array element for states, 5th for transitions) holding the romanized reading.
suitable_for: any concept with a neutral midpoint and two opposing extremes

templates.description: Logographic variant of ROM-CV-BI. Same inverted-bell-curve geometry with flat shoulders, normal-state line at 50% page height, and bottom-centre nadir for the most intense state. Uses the 4-level click cycle (TLR default → TL script → SL → Quiz) on both States textboxes and the directly-draggable Transitions sliding text.
templates.notes: Same usage principles as ROM-CV-BI — bottom point is always the most intense/negative state. Each conceptData/transitionsData item carries an additional TLR field (6th array element for states, 5th for transitions) holding the romanized reading. Sliding text drag is direct (no hit-area rectangle), matching the GTCV.html pattern.
suitable_for: any concept with one clear most-intense state reached via a process

templates.description: Logographic clock template with grammar-plugin architecture. SL and TL each supply their own time-expression grammar functions (formatExact, formatApprox). TL boxes show TLR by default; click toggles to TL script.
templates.notes: Most complex template — requires grammar function authoring, not just vocabulary substitution. See LANG config block for full documentation.
